anatomy.intro: Long hairlike spines surround the flexible stems, with growing tips at the ends of the hanging tails.

parts.function: The green cylinder stores water and carries the trailing growth.
parts.label: Pendant stem

parts.function: Long pale spines create the shaggy surface around the stem.
parts.label: Hairlike spines

parts.function: Repeated growth points bear spines and can produce flowers.
parts.label: Areole

parts.function: New tissue extends the lower end of the hanging stem.
parts.label: Growing tip

flowers.text: Red to pink flowers emerge from the stem sides; the collection has an observed red-orange bloom. Their asymmetrical base holds nectar in a swollen spur, attracting hummingbirds.

growth.note: Track recovery by the diameter, hair density, and spacing of spines on the newest tips.

stages.text: Young growth initially makes a compact fingerlike shoot.
stages.title: Short stem

stages.text: Lengthening stems arch over an edge and hang downward.
stages.title: Trailing tail

stages.text: An established plant can carry side-borne flowers among the hairs.
stages.title: Flowering cascade

habitat.text: Monkey tail cactus grows on Bolivian rock faces. Huntington records the type locality at Cerro El Fraile, Florida Province, at 2,000 m. Its pendant stems naturally hang into the open space below their rooting points.

No flowers, grafts, or roots. Numbers must remain readable at 350px. Generic anatomical specimen, not measurement evidence. Monkey tail cactus Cleistocactus colademononis: two long gracefully hanging cylindrical green stems thickly covered with long soft white hairlike spines, rooted base emerges over a small neutral rock ledge at upper left, not a pot. 1 points to the green cylindrical pendant stem visible between hair; 2 to the long white hairlike spines; 3 to a small spine-bearing areole visible through a thinner patch of hair; 4 to the rounded growing tip at the lower end of a tail. No flowers.

lookalikes.name: Compact woolly Espostoa
lookalikes.text: Espostoa stays upright with dense wool around a column; monkey tail naturally hangs and has long hairlike spines.

mature.text: Cultivated stems can trail about 1 m, creating a hanging curtain that needs clear space below the pot.

milestones.text: Acquired from Gerych's Design as part of the cactus planter now tracked as P19.
milestones.title: Arrived in the shared planter

nameStory.text: Residents near Samaipata already called it cola de mono, or monkey's tail, before its botanical description in 2003.
